The relative orientation of the terminal methyl and hydroxymethyl branches was evaluated; conformers maintaining C...C branch distances >2.7 Å avoid unfavorable gauche/eclipsed strain. Conformers ranked highest (e.g., 4, 14, 1, 20) form compact, low-strain structures with multiple heavy-atom pairs in the ideal H-bonding window, effectively neutralizing dipole penalties. Mid-ranked conformers adopt moderately extended shapes or possess only isolated interactions without major steric defects. The lowest stability entries exhibit either highly unfavorable stretched geometries (poor dipole screening), compressed functional group proximities (<2.6 Å indicating repulsion), or crowded methyl/hydroxyl overlaps. Subtle energy differences were resolved by favoring conformers that simultaneously maximize H-bond count and minimize branch eclipsing.
